Subject: RE: Sudden token delays on /v1/generate — triage notes (prelim)

Quick triage notes — sending what we have so far:

- Symptom: p99 jump ~+2.3s starting 14:28 PDT; overall token throughput stable.
- Correlated signal: elevated cache misses (KV prefix cache) across several serving shards beginning at 14:26 PDT. Miss ratio rose from ~2.7% to ~41%.
- Recent change: a routing policy tweak rolled at 14:20 that shifted a subset of traffic to model-v2-latency-optimized; that variant has a different KV key distribution which appears to have triggered aggressive eviction patterns.

Immediate recommended mitigations (I can action within 10m):
1) Rollback routing tweak to previous policy (safe, reversible) — expected to reduce cache churn quickly.
2) Temporarily increase KV cache size parameter on affected shards (+25%) and enable prefix-warmup for busy prefixes.
3) Add short-term traffic steering: route Finovate traffic to model-v1-stable (slower model but warmer cache) while we validate.

I attached a csv slice of cache metrics and a short incident triage PDF.

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: kv-cache-metrics.csv, incident_triage-notes.pdf

Subject: Customer status: We’ve identified a cache churn issue and are applying mitigations

Alex — quick status for Finovate users:

Summary: We observed a sudden increase in KV cache misses that has caused token p99 regressions for a subset of requests. Our SRE and runtime teams have identified a recent routing policy change as a likely trigger.

Immediate actions in progress:
- Rolling back the routing tweak for impacted traffic to restore warm cache behavior (in progress).
- Increasing KV cache size on targeted shards and enabling prefix-warmup.
- Steering your traffic to model-v1-stable for the next hour to avoid rewarming penalties.

What we need from Finovate: please pause or throttle any batch/non-essential jobs for 60 minutes if possible. That will reduce cache churn while we stabilize.

ETA: we expect measurable improvement within 15 minutes of the rollback and full stabilization within 1 hour. We will follow up with metrics and a postmortem.

If you prefer a short call, I’m available now — otherwise I’ll provide the next update at +30m.

Regards,

Subject: Incident update: mitigations applied, p95/p99 improving, next steps

Update: the rollback and cache-size bump were applied 09:02 PDT on 9/14 after a controlled window in staging. Observed effects:
- p95 dropped back to ~130ms (from ~1.1s).
- p99 reduced to ~210ms (from ~2.6s).
- KV miss ratio returned to baseline (~3%).

Actions completed:
- Routing policy rollback executed (INF-4721).
- KV cache size increased +25% on targeted shards; prefix-warmup enabled.
- No OOM or stability events observed after 2 hours of traffic.

Next steps / product asks (for roadmap & console features):
1) Expose KV eviction/miss heatmap in Redwood Console for per-customer views (high priority for customer visibility).
2) Add an automated warmup mode for new model variants or routing changes (configurable per deployment).
3) Implement an alerting rule for sudden rise in prefix-miss-rate to auto-trigger safe fallback routing.

Postmortem: I’ll schedule a follow-up for Wednesday to capture timeline + RCA. Jonas/Karthik — please capture how the variant’s key distribution differs and whether we can add a deterministic check during canary rollout.

Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
